blocks.source: De profundis clamavi ad te, Domine: Domine, exaudi vocem meam: Fiant aures tuae intendentes, in vocem deprecationis meae. Si iniquitates observaveris, Domine: Domine, quis sustinebit? Quia apud te propitiatio est: et propter legem tuam sustinui te, Domine. Sustinuit anima mea in verbo eius: speravit anima mea in Domino. A custodia matutina usque ad noctem: speret Israel in Domino. Quia apud Dominum misericordia: et copiosa apud eum redemptio. Et ipse redimet Israel, ex omnibus iniquitatibus eius. Gloria Patri, et Filio, et Spiritui Sancto. Sicut erat in principio, et nunc, et semper, et in saecula saeculorum. Amen.
blocks.english: Out of the depths have I cried unto Thee, O Lord. Lord, hear my voice. O, let Thine ears be attentive to the voice of my supplication. If thou, O Lord, wilt observe iniquities, Lord, who shall stand it? For with Thee there is merciful forgiveness; and by reason of Thy law I have waited for Thee, O Lord. My soul hath relied on His word. My soul hath hoped in the Lord. From the morning watch even until night, let Israel hope in the Lord. For with the Lord there is mercy, and with Him plentiful redemption. And He shall redeem Israel from all his iniquities. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

blocks.source: Domine, non est exaltatum cor meum: neque elati sunt oculi mei. Neque ambulavi in magnis: neque in mirabilibus super me. Si non humiliter sentiebam: sed exaltavi animam meam: Sicut ablactatus est super matre sua, ita retributio in anima mea. Speret Israel in Domino, ex hoc nunc et usque in saeculum. Gloria Patri, et Filio, et Spiritui Sancto. Sicut erat in principio, et nunc, et semper, et in saecula saeculorum. Amen.
blocks.english: O Lord, my heart is not lifted up; nor are mine eyes lofty. Neither do I walk in great matters, nor in things too wonderful me. If I had not been humbly minded, but have lifted up my soul, As a child that is weaned upon his mother’s breast, so let my reward be in my soul. Let Israel hope in the Lord, from this time forth for evermore. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

editorialNotes.text: Prime: The PDF prints “Deus, qui virginalem aulam” in Latin but the English of “Deus, qui salutis aeternae.” These are different collects. Both printed texts are retained here; this pairing requires editorial resolution.
Terce: The two seasonal English collects at Terce are reversed relative to the Latin in the PDF. This row retains the printed “Outside Advent” texts, which are different collects.
Terce: The two seasonal English collects at Terce are reversed relative to the Latin in the PDF. This row retains the printed “During Advent” texts, which are different collects.
Sext: The English column includes the Kyrie after this response; the Latin column omits it. No Latin has been added.

Vespers: The supplied English of “Quando natus es” changes to wording from a different antiphon (“bestowed upon us His Godhead”). The PDF’s differing texts are retained; this is not an exact translation of the Latin.
Matins: The PDF prints “Domine, labia ✠ea aperies,” with an incomplete Latin word. The printed source and its supplied English are retained.

Matins: The English column omits the repeated Advent absolution and first blessing. Their English below is reused from the identical Latin prayers and supplied English earlier in Matins (pp. 114–115); the heading is already English in the source column.
Matins: The English column repeats “The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee…” after this versicle; that repetition is absent from the Latin column at this point. Both printed versions are retained.
Lauds: The English incipit labels “O wondrous union” as “from Christmas until Advent”; the Latin column says “from Christmas to Candlemas.” Both printed labels are retained.
Lauds: The supplied English of “Quando natus es” changes to wording from another antiphon. Both printed versions are retained; they are not equivalent translations.
Lauds: The Latin Psalm 62 ends its psalm text after “partes vulpium erunt”; the English includes the additional verse beginning “But the king shall rejoice in God.” No absent Latin has been added.
Lauds: The English canticle includes “O ye spirits and souls of the just” and “O ye holy and humble of heart”; the Latin column omits these invocations. Both printed versions are retained.
Lauds: The PDF itself repeats these versicles in English within the Latin column. That duplication is retained.
Lauds: Only three seasonal Marian anthems are printed here: Ave Regina caelorum, Regina caeli, and Salve Regina. Alma Redemptoris Mater is absent from this office in the PDF and has not been added.

All eight hours have been compared with both columns of PDF pages 105–163. Source discrepancies are retained and identified rather than silently corrected. Seasonal and weekday alternatives remain inline for now; the office is not marked ready for publication while conflicting readings and reference assembly remain unresolved.
